name: Netdryrun
summary: Netdryrun dry-runs a network change in a real containerlab lab before it reaches production, and returns a verdict with evidence. verify_change (0.4, FRR): declare what you intend to change; anything else that changes in the routing state fails the run.

use_cases.when: Before proposing or applying a routing or policy change, when the lab has checks (netdryrun.yml) that state what must hold.
use_cases.does: Deploys the containerlab lab with the change, waits for convergence, runs every check, destroys the lab. A pass covers only what the checks look at.

use_cases.when: When no checks exist and a ticket states what the change is meant to do: declare that intent, and anything else that changes in the routing state fails.
use_cases.does: Boots the lab with the before configs and with the after configs, snapshots sessions, routes of every protocol, every BGP path and every advertisement, and fails on any difference the intent doesn't declare. An approval needs each side booted twice with identical snapshots.
use_cases.cli: netdryrun verify topology.clab.yml --before main --after HEAD --intent netdryrun-intent.yml --json report.json

use_cases.when: No checks and no stated intent: capture today's behavior as checks, then run them against the change.
use_cases.does: Reads sessions and routes from a lab and returns checks as YAML; writes nothing.

use_cases.when: Before a run: check a netdryrun.yml and its topology without starting a lab.

prerequisites: Linux, or Windows with WSL2; not macOS
Docker and containerlab, with root-equivalent rights (labs run privileged containers)
Python 3.10 to 3.14 (pipx install netdryrun, or uvx netdryrun mcp)
Not inside a sandbox without Docker-in-Docker; there, open a pull request and let the GitHub Action run it
Images: FRR and SR Linux are public; SONiC needs docker-sonic-vs; Arista EOS needs your own cEOS image
A lab of the network (a containerlab topology and its configs); Netdryrun never connects to real devices
limits: A pass of dry_run covers only what the checks look at; behavior no check covers is not tested.

verify_change covers the observed control-plane state of the lab (BGP sessions, routes of every protocol, every BGP path, advertised and received routes), nothing else: no data plane beyond ping checks.
verify_change is FRR only in 0.4; the topology must be identical on both sides.
verify_change: an intent explains what it declares, leaks included; the intent must come from the ticket or the operator, never from the diff.

verify_change: received routes are compared before inbound policy without their communities (FRR doesn't list them there); a default-originate advertisement is compared by presence, not by its attributes.
verify_change: IPv4 and IPv6 unicast only; sessions carrying other address families, and unnumbered BGP neighbors, are refused (exit 2).

Settle and hold stretch to the longest BGP advertisement interval a driver reads, except on Arista EOS, where a configured out-delay is not read yet: raise --settle and --hold above it there (planned for 0.4.1).
A route that crosses several peers with long advertisement intervals can take one interval per hop, and update-delay is not read: raise --settle for those.
A lab whose state never settles gives INCONCLUSIVE (exit 3): this says nothing about the change; retry at most once, then escalate.
afi: evpn is refused on Arista EOS and Nokia SR Linux.

verify_change does not observe nodes passed as unobserved (hosts), IGP adjacency state (OSPF and IS-IS routes are compared, their adjacencies are not), or the data plane beyond a standing guard's ping checks: an undeclared change there does not fail.
record covers every active VRF on FRR and SONiC; on Nokia SR Linux and Arista EOS it records the default VRF only, with a warning.

SR Linux: `bgp_prefixes` counts the neighbor's `received-routes`, which on SR Linux 26.7.2 includes routes that fail BGP loop detection and are not usable. On a live capture of `examples/srl-frr` on 2026-10-28 the counter read 3 where one prefix was usable and `rejected-routes` read 0. A `min` or `exact` prefix check on SR Linux can pass on a count that includes unusable routes. The test data above predates that capture; it has not yet been re-captured. Mitigation: pair the count with `route` checks for the prefixes that matter. Fix scheduled: 0.4.1.

SR Linux: graceful restart: a stale path (a restarting peer's route, kept until it re-sends it or the stale timer ends) counts as present and best; no stale marker is read yet. A route check can pass on a route that is about to go. Mitigation: leave graceful restart off in the lab, or use a `timeout` above the stale timer. Fix scheduled: 0.4.1.

SONiC: graceful restart: a stale path (a restarting peer's route, kept until it re-sends it or the stale timer ends) counts as present and best; no stale marker is read yet. A route check can pass on a route that is about to go. Mitigation: leave graceful restart off in the lab, or use a `timeout` above the stale timer. Fix scheduled: 0.4.1.

Arista EOS: graceful restart: a stale path (a restarting peer's route, kept until it re-sends it or the stale timer ends) counts as present and best; no stale marker is read yet. A route check can pass on a route that is about to go. Mitigation: leave graceful restart off in the lab, or use a `timeout` above the stale timer. Fix scheduled: 0.4.1.

Juniper (beta): Hidden routes count as received, except routes Junos hid because the import policy rejected them (`hidden-reason` "Rejected by import policy"): those can never be used, and FRR and Arista EOS don't keep them at all.
Juniper (beta): `bgp_route` reads routes received over BGP only. Junos doesn't list its own static, direct or aggregate routes as BGP routes, even when an export policy advertises them.
Juniper (beta): `bgp_prefixes` reads Junos's `accepted-prefix-count`, which also leaves out received routes Junos can't use (an unusable next hop); FRR counts those.
Juniper (beta): Link and node faults on a cJunosEvolved node and `inject_routes` from it are refused before deploying.

Juniper (beta): Every deploy installs Junos in the VM: about 4 minutes to a CLI on a quiet 20-thread host, up to 19 minutes with a CPU-heavy job beside it. Set `CPTX_NUM_IF` (see the example) and a check `timeout` that covers the boot.

platforms.name: Arista EOS (cEOS, bring your own image)
Juniper cJunosEvolved (beta, bring your own image)

install: claude mcp add netdryrun -- netdryrun mcp

run: CHECKS PASSED (only what the checks cover)
INCONCLUSIVE: the lab did not reach a testable state; this says nothing about your change. Do not apply it until a run passes.

verify.1: failed (undeclared changes, a declaration that didn't happen, or a failed standing guard)

never: sends telemetry or uploads anything by default (the GitHub Action's reserved cloud input is off)
writes or weakens checks or intents for you
